basic_information.official_title: AN ACT ESTABLISHING IN THE MUNICIPALITY OF NORTHERN KABUNTALAN, PROVINCE OF MAGUINDANAO DEL NORTE, A LEVEL I GENERAL HOSPITAL TO BE KNOWN AS THE NORTHERN KABUNTALAN GENERAL HOSPITAL, AND APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR
signed_by: Prof. Raby B. Angkal, Secretary General
basic_information.effectivity: 15 days after completion of publication in a newspaper of general circulation in the BARMM

citizen_summary.what_is_this_about: Establishes a 25-bed Level 1 general hospital in Northern Kabuntalan, Maguindanao del Norte — and sets out a staged plan to hand its financial management from the regional health ministry to the municipality once the municipality proves it can run it.
citizen_summary.why_was_it_proposed: To put a general hospital in the municipality, and to build local capacity to manage it rather than leaving it permanently regional.
citizen_summary.what_will_change: A Level 1 hospital with 25 beds is created under the Ministry of Health, which initially takes full responsibility for its budget, procurement and expenditure — then transfers that to the local government in stages, against benchmarks.
who_will_be_affected: The municipal local government, which is to take over financial management in stages
The Ministry of Health, which runs it first and assesses the handover
citizen_summary.when_will_it_take_effect: In force since 2025 — 15 days after completion of publication.

what_this_means_for_you.in_short: NOW LAW. A 25-bed Level 1 hospital for Northern Kabuntalan — run financially by the regional health ministry at first, then handed to the municipality step by step as it proves it can manage it.
in_practice: A Level 1 general hospital with 25-bed capacity in Northern Kabuntalan
Under the administrative supervision of the Ministry of Health – BARMM
The site is determined jointly by MOH-BARMM and the municipal local government, in consultation with other LGUs and stakeholders
MOH-BARMM must formulate operational guidelines within 90 days of effectivity
MOH-BARMM assumes full responsibility for financial management — budget, procurement and expenditures
A phased transition plan gradually transfers financial administration to the municipality, with benchmarks
Full financial control passes to the LGU only after assessments of governance, accountability and sustainability
₱50,000,000 initial, from the Miscellaneous and Personnel Benefit Fund of the 2025 Bangsamoro budget

for_specific_groups.Residents: A general hospital in the municipality, run to Level 1 standards.
for_specific_groups.The municipal government: You do not get the hospital's finances immediately — control transfers in stages, and only after MOH assessments of your accounting standards, procurement practice and budgetary discipline.
for_specific_groups.Anyone watching devolution: This is one of the few acts that sets out a capacity-tested handover rather than devolving or centralising outright.

what_this_means_for_you.when_you_will_feel_it: In force since 2025; delivery depends on the appropriation being released.
what_you_can_do: Ask MOH-BARMM for the operational guidelines, due within 90 days of effectivity
Ask what stage the phased transition has reached and what benchmarks were set
watch_out_for: The act sets no deadline for completing the transfer to the LGU, and no consequence if it never happens.
The benchmarks for assessing LGU capacity are not specified in the act.
Section 3 refers to consulting the LGUs of the Province of Maguindanao del Sur, although the municipality is in Maguindanao del Norte — an apparent drafting error in the enacted text.

key_terms_explained.Level 1 hospital: A basic facility — emergency care, general medicine, a small ward.
key_terms_explained.Phased transition plan: A staged handover, here of financial management from the regional ministry to the municipality.
key_terms_explained.Benchmarks: Standards the LGU must meet before taking on more financial control.
key_terms_explained.MPBF: Miscellaneous and Personnel Benefit Fund — the budget line the initial ₱50 million comes from.

what_this_means_for_you.status_note: Passed Jumada Al-Akhirah 11, 1446 / 12 December 2024, approved by the Chief Minister on 9 January 2025.

benefits.headline: A 25-bed hospital, plus a staged plan to put it under local control.

direct_benefits.benefit: A Level 1 general hospital with 25 beds

for_citizens: None. The act imposes no duty on the public.

what_is_prohibited: The act defines no prohibited acts and creates no offences.

penalties.for_citizens: None. The act creates no offence, fine or imprisonment.

where_to_complain.oversight: Ministry of Health – BARMM, which supervises the hospital and holds financial responsibility until transfer
where_to_complain.note: The act creates no complaints procedure of its own.

everyday_scenarios: A resident asks who pays for the hospital. At the start, the regional health ministry handles budget, procurement and expenditure in full; over time, and only if the municipality passes MOH assessments, that shifts to the LGU.
The municipality asks when it will control the hospital. Section 4 makes that depend on demonstrated financial management capacity, with no fixed date.

key_provisions: Section 1 — Establishes a Level 1 general hospital with 25-bed capacity in the Municipality of Northern Kabuntalan, Maguindanao del Norte, to be known as the Northern Kabuntalan General Hospital (NKGH).

Section 2 — The hospital is under the administrative supervision of MOH-BARMM, which determines and approves its organisational structure, formulates guidelines for its operation as a Level 1 hospital, and ensures funding for construction of the hospital building and other complementary infrastructure, facilities and medical equipment, as well as maintenance and personnel services costs.

Section 3 — MOH-BARMM, in coordination with the local government unit of Northern Kabuntalan, jointly determines the site of the hospital, in consultation with LGUs of the province and other relevant stakeholders.

Section 4 — MOH-BARMM shall formulate operational guidelines within 90 days of effectivity, and assumes full responsibility for the financial management of the NKGH including budget allocation, procurement and expenditures. A phased transition plan shall be developed and implemented to gradually transfer financial administration and management to the LGU of Northern Kabuntalan, in stages, with benchmarks established to assess the LGU's capacity. MOH-BARMM shall conduct regular evaluations of whether the LGU has demonstrated sufficient financial management capacity, including compliance with accounting standards, efficient procurement practices and budgetary discipline. Full financial control passes to the LGU only upon successful completion of assessments focused on local governance, accountability and sustainability of healthcare service delivery.

Section 5 — An initial ₱50,000,000 is charged against the Miscellaneous and Personnel Benefit Fund of the 2025 General Appropriation Act of the Bangsamoro, with subsequent operations funded through the annual appropriations.
Section 8 — Takes effect 15 days after completion of publication in a newspaper of general circulation in the BARMM.

citizen_questions.a: At first the Ministry of Health – BARMM takes full responsibility for budget allocation, procurement and expenditures. It then transfers financial administration to the municipality in phases, once assessments show the LGU can manage it.

citizen_questions.q: When does the municipality take over?
citizen_questions.a: The act sets no date. Transfer happens in stages against benchmarks, and full financial control passes only after successful assessments of governance, accountability and sustainability.

citizen_questions.q: Where will the hospital be built?
citizen_questions.a: The site is determined jointly by MOH-BARMM and the municipal LGU, in consultation with other LGUs and relevant stakeholders.

citizen_questions.q: How much money, and from where?
citizen_questions.a: An initial ₱50 million from the Miscellaneous and Personnel Benefit Fund of the 2025 Bangsamoro budget.
